claims.claim: A randomised trial of nearly 12,000 older adults found that personalised exercise recommendations integrated into primary care reduced documented falls and fall-related injuries.
claims.episode_span: A randomised trial in the United States found that personalised exercise recommendations integrated into primary care reduced documented falls and fall-related injuries.
claims.source_title: Simple Exercise Programme Found to Reduce Falls and Injuries in Older Adults: Study
claims.supporting_quote: A randomised trial involving nearly 12,000 older adults found that personalised exercise recommendations integrated into primary care reduced documented falls and fall-related injuries.

claims.claim: University of Wisconsin-Madison researchers published a review in Cell Press Blue in August 2026 on protein and amino-acid restriction and aging.
claims.episode_span: Researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison published a review in Cell Press Blue in August 2026 on lowering dietary protein, or particular amino acids, while still meeting nutritional needs.
claims.source_title: Research Review Examines How Protein Intake May Influence Aging
claims.supporting_quote: Researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison had their new review published in Cell Press Blue in August 2026.

claims.claim: In laboratory animals, lower-protein diets have extended lifespan and improved metabolic health, in some cases without reducing total calories.
claims.episode_span: In laboratory animals, including yeast, flies, and rodents, lower-protein diets have extended lifespan and improved metabolic measures, sometimes without cutting total calories
claims.source_title: Research Review Examines How Protein Intake May Influence Aging
claims.supporting_quote: In laboratory animals, lower-protein diets have extended lifespan and improved metabolic health measures. Some benefits occurred without reducing total calorie intake, suggesting that dietary composition plays a role.

claims.claim: A trial described in the protein review found that people on a low-protein diet for 43 days lost body weight and fat and had lower fasting blood sugar despite eating more calories.
claims.episode_span: One trial in the review found that people on a low-protein diet for 43 days lost body weight and fat and had lower fasting blood sugar despite eating more calories.
claims.source_title: Research Review Examines How Protein Intake May Influence Aging
claims.supporting_quote: One trial described in the review found that people consuming a low-protein diet for 43 days lost body weight and fat and had lower fasting blood sugar despite eating more calories.

claims.claim: A five-week low-protein intervention in lean men improved insulin sensitivity, and whether protein restriction extends human lifespan remains unknown.
claims.episode_span: A five-week intervention in lean men improved insulin sensitivity.
claims.source_title: Research Review Examines How Protein Intake May Influence Aging
claims.supporting_quote: Another five-week intervention in lean men improved insulin sensitivity, meaning their bodies responded more effectively to the hormone that helps regulate blood sugar.

claims.claim: FGF21 rises in response to protein restriction in humans and rodents.
claims.episode_span: Fibroblast growth factor 21 rises with protein restriction in humans and rodents.
claims.source_title: Research Review Examines How Protein Intake May Influence Aging
claims.supporting_quote: This hormone rises in response to protein restriction in humans and rodents.

claims.claim: Seventeen of 4,265 plasma proteins were associated with all-cause mortality in 1,025 LonGenity participants over a mean follow-up of 8.05 years, with replication in 1,124 BLSA participants.
claims.episode_span: Seventeen proteins were significantly associated with all-cause mortality, and the associations were checked in 1,124 participants from the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging.
claims.source_title: Identifying Plasma Proteins Associated with Mortality Risk and Biological Age
claims.supporting_quote: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 1,025 older adults from the LonGenity study , analyzing 4,265 plasma proteins. Associations between protein levels and all-cause mortality were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression over a mean follow-up of 8.05 years.

claims.claim: Higher ERBB1 and ANTXR2 were associated with lower mortality and younger biological age, while higher GDF15, HE4, and IGFBP-2 were associated with higher mortality and older biological age.
claims.episode_span: Higher epidermal growth factor receptor (ERBB1) and anthrax toxin receptor 2 (ANTXR2) tracked with lower mortality risk and a younger proteomic biological age across multiple organ systems.
claims.source_title: Identifying Plasma Proteins Associated with Mortality Risk and Biological Age
claims.supporting_quote: Higher levels of epidermal growth factor receptor (ERBB1) and anthrax toxin receptor 2 (ANTXR2) were associated with lower mortality risk and younger biological age across multiple organ systems.

claims.claim: A 24-year study of more than 8,200 adults linked excess body weight to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making, especially after age 65.
claims.episode_span: A 24-year observational study of more than 8,200 adults linked excess body weight with faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making, with the connection particularly strong after age 65.
claims.source_title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think
claims.supporting_quote: A major 24-year study involving more than 8,200 adults suggests that excess body weight may accelerate brain aging, leading to faster declines in memory, concentration, and decision-making skills.

claims.claim: A randomised crossover trial of 31 adults aged 60 to 75 found improved brain insulin responsiveness in memory-related right-hemisphere regions after 16 weeks of daily unsalted skin-roasted peanuts.
claims.episode_span: After the peanut period, insulin responsiveness improved in memory-related regions of the right hemisphere, including portions of the lingual gyrus, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, and posterior cingulate gyrus.
claims.source_title: Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day
claims.supporting_quote: After participants consumed peanuts daily for 16 weeks, researchers observed improved insulin responsiveness in a group of brain regions in the right hemisphere.

claims.claim: A 2025 study by Peter Joris found that 16 weeks of peanut consumption increased cerebral blood flow by 3.6 percent and verbal memory by 5.8 percent.
claims.episode_span: An earlier 2025 study by the same senior author, Peter Joris, found that 16 weeks of peanut consumption raised overall cerebral blood flow by 3.6 percent and verbal memory performance by 5.8 percent.
claims.source_title: Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day
claims.supporting_quote: That investigation found that consuming peanuts for 16 weeks increased overall cerebral blood flow (CBF) by 3.6% and improved verbal memory performance by 5.8%.

claims.claim: Lipid-nanoparticle delivery of circular RNA encoding OCT4, SOX2, and KLF4 rejuvenated senescent mesenchymal stem cells without converting them to induced pluripotent stem cells by an ESRG assay.
claims.episode_span: Using droplet digital PCR for the pluripotency marker ESRG, they found that this delivery alone did not turn the cells into induced pluripotent stem cells.
claims.source_title: Circular RNA Encoding Yamanaka Factors Enables Partial Reprogramming Without Pluripotency
claims.supporting_quote: Using a rigorously validated droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) system targeting the pluripotency marker ESRG , we demonstrated that circ-OSK delivery alone is insufficient to transform MSCs into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs).

claims.claim: BTEC, trained on 553 healthy breast samples, correlated with chronological age at 0.91 with a mean absolute error of 3.0 years and outperformed Horvath and Hannum clocks in breast tissue.
claims.episode_span: DNA methylation measured in 553 healthy breast-tissue samples produced a tissue-specific clock, called BTEC, whose age estimates correlated with chronological age at 0.91 and missed by a mean absolute error of 3.0 years
claims.source_title: A breast tissue-specific epigenetic clock provides accurate chronological age predictions and reveals de-correlation of age and DNA methylation in tumor-adjacent and tumor samples
claims.supporting_quote: BTEC significantly outperformed existing clocks, demonstrating superior correlation with chronological age ( r  = 0.91) and lower prediction errors (MAE = 3.0 y) without requiring dataset-specific regressions adjustments.

claims.claim: BTEC predictions were about 2.3 years younger in tumor-adjacent breast samples and 14 to 15 years younger in tumors, with greater distortion in HER2-positive and triple-negative tumors than in hormone-receptor-positive tumors.
claims.episode_span: In tumor-adjacent breast samples the clock ran 2.3 years younger than chronological age on average, and in tumor samples the gap was 14 to 15 years.
claims.source_title: A breast tissue-specific epigenetic clock provides accurate chronological age predictions and reveals de-correlation of age and DNA methylation in tumor-adjacent and tumor samples
claims.supporting_quote: BTEC's chronological age predictions for tumor-adjacent samples showed distortions, with an average deviation of -2.3 y, which was even more pronounced in tumor samples, where the average difference between predicted and chronological age was -14 to -15 y.

claims.claim: A six-CpG saliva epigenetic clock had mean absolute errors of 3.240 and 3.267 years and lower error than 85 percent of 60 previously published saliva clocks.
claims.episode_span: The six-CpG saliva models, using robust Lasso and support vector regression, had mean absolute errors of 3.240 and 3.267 years in development
claims.source_title: Development of a precise saliva-based epigenetic clock using a six-CpG-marker panel
claims.supporting_quote: Among the models tested, rLasso and SVR delivered the best and comparable predictive accuracy, with MAEs of 3.240 and 3.267 years, respectively, which were significantly better than the other linear models.

claims.claim: A systematic review found that Hannum, Horvath, Levine, and GrimAge clocks tend to agree in direction but vary in size, and that BMI, HIV infection, and male sex were associated with clock acceleration.
claims.episode_span: Higher body mass index, HIV infection, and male sex were associated with acceleration of one or more clocks.
claims.source_title: A systematic review of biological, social and environmental factors associated with epigenetic clock acceleration
claims.supporting_quote: We found that the Horvath, Hannum, Levine and GrimAge epigenetic clocks tend to agree in direction of effects, but vary in size. Body mass index, HIV infection, and male sex were significantly associated with acceleration of one or more epigenetic clocks.

claims.claim: Each five-year increase in DNA methylation age was associated with an 8 to 15 percent increased risk of mortality in a meta-analysis of 23 articles and 41,607 participants.
claims.episode_span: each five-year increase in DNA methylation age was associated with an 8 to 15 percent higher risk of death.
claims.source_title: The epigenetic clock as a predictor of disease and mortality risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.supporting_quote: Meta-analyses indicated that each 5-year increase in DNA methylation age was associated an 8 to 15% increased risk of mortality.

claims.claim: A 391-CpG skin and blood methylation clock detected epigenetic age acceleration in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria fibroblasts below the sensitivity of other clocks and rose with proliferation in culture.
claims.episode_span: the skin-and-blood clock detected epigenetic age acceleration in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria fibroblasts at a magnitude other methylation clocks were not sensitive enough to see.
claims.source_title: Epigenetic clock for skin and blood cells applied to Hutchinson Gilford Progeria Syndrome and ex vivo studies
claims.supporting_quote: When used on fibroblasts from Hutchinson Gilford Progeria Syndrome patients, this age estimator (referred to as the skin & blood clock) uncovered an epigenetic age acceleration with a magnitude that is below the sensitivity levels of other DNAm-based biomarkers.

claims.claim: DNA methylation clocks can estimate age across tissues and the life course and are described as linking developmental and maintenance processes to biological aging.
claims.episode_span: Methylation clocks can estimate age across the life course and are proposed as links between development, maintenance, and biological aging: review.
claims.source_title: DNA methylation-based biomarkers and the epigenetic clock theory of ageing
claims.supporting_quote: These 'epigenetic clocks' link developmental and maintenance processes to biological ageing, giving rise to a unified theory of life course.
